_note: UPDATED 2026-09-27, superseding the 2026-09-22 operator-stated figures below (previous values: OR 0.251, CT 0.10, NM 0.059, NY 0.055, KY 0.0285) with rates cited to each state's own published schedule/statute, supplied alongside the Q3 2026 IFTA rate reference (config/ifta_rates_q3_2026.json) built for this same purpose. NM changed materially (0.059 -> 0.04378); KY, CT, OR are effectively unchanged (rounding only); NY tightened from 0.055 to 0.0546. These five states each run their own WEIGHT-DISTANCE or highway-use tax on heavy trucks, charged per mile on top of (Oregon: instead of) standard IFTA fuel tax: Oregon's Weight-Mile Tax, Connecticut's Highway Use Fee, New Mexico's Weight-Distance Tax, New York's Highway Use Tax (HUT), and Kentucky's KYU (Weight Distance Tax). All rates are for an 80,000-lb, 5-axle interstate tractor-trailer -- actual per-truck rates are tiered by declared/registered weight, so a truck registered below 80,000 lbs would owe a lower rate than shown here; this is a fleet-wide approximation, not a truck-specific one.
OR_note: Table A, 78,001-80,000 lb bracket, $0.2512/mi (oregon.gov ODOT). Oregon ALSO has real, filed weight-mile tax returns in this corpus (ingest/parse_oregon.py, analysis/oregon_gap.py) for ZONE and partially for XTRACK -- cost_structure.oregon_per_mile() uses those REAL figures where a filed return exists, and only falls back to this schedule rate x mile-share estimate where it does not (XTRACK's gap quarters, AFG entirely -- AFG has no Oregon account on record). Filing is monthly by default; quarterly if elected/approved.
CT_note: Connecticut's Highway Use Fee: $0.10/mi at 78,001-80,000 lb, but $0.175/mi at 80,001 lb and over (portal.ct.gov/drs) -- this config prices the 80,000-lb bracket only; a truck actually registered above 80,000 lb owes the higher rate and is not covered by this single number. Charged on vehicles over 26,000 lbs gross weight, separate from the CT diesel IFTA fuel tax. Filing is QUARTERLY (corrected 2026-09-27 -- an earlier note here said monthly).
KY_note: KYU applies to vehicles over 59,999 lbs, flat $0.0285 per Kentucky mile regardless of declared weight above that threshold (transportation.ky.gov). Filed quarterly. This is the SAME rate already reported separately as KY's IFTA surcharge in config/ifta_rates_q3_2026.json -- the two files describe the same $0.0285/gal-of-taxable-gallons-equivalent charge from two different angles (per Kentucky mile here; per Kentucky-taxable-gallon there) and must not both be added to a single truck's cost.
NM_note: New Mexico's Weight Distance Tax: 43.78 mills/mile ($0.04378/mi) for the 78,001 lb and over ('full-haul') bracket (realfile.tax.newmexico.gov/mvd10964.pdf) -- a reduced rate exists for qualifying one-way-haul vehicles, not used here since this fleet runs standard OTR dry van/reefer. Filed quarterly.
NY_note: New York's Highway Use Tax, gross-weight method, Schedule 1, 78,001-80,000 lb, LADEN, non-Thruway miles: $0.0546/mi (tax.ny.gov MT-903 instructions). Unladen miles and Schedule 2 (currently $0.039/mi at this weight) are NOT the same rate -- this config is a conservative single-rate estimate for internal costing, not a substitute for splitting laden/unladen/Thruway miles on the actual MT-903 filing. Filing frequency (monthly/quarterly/annual) depends on the carrier's own prior-year HUT liability.
source: State-published rate schedules/statutes as of 2026-09-27 (Oregon ODOT Table A, CT DRS HUF page, Kentucky Transportation Cabinet KYU page, New Mexico MVD-10964, NY DTF MT-903 instructions) -- see config/ifta_rates_q3_2026.json's per-state special_mileage_tax.source fields for the exact URL used for each. Superseded the 2026-09-22 operator-stated figures, which were themselves sourced from a blank Illinois MFUT-15 calculator template rather than each state's own page.
